import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the dataset
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type

Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the bubble chart
# X-axis: Megapixels (a key feature)
# Y-axis: Price (a key outcome)
# Bubble Size: Weight of the camera (an important physical attribute)
# Color: Sensor Type (a critical technical specification)
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    size='weight_grams',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis',
    sizes=(200, 2500),
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Add annotations for clarity, as the dataset is small ---
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    ax.text(
        x=df['megapixels'][i],
        y=df['price_usd'][i] + 150, # Offset text slightly above the bubble
        s=f"{df['brand'][i]}\n({df['model_year'][i]})",
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=11, ha='center')
    )

# --- Customize the plot for professional presentation ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title and subtitle

# Set informative axis labels

ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Format the y-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%,.0f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Set logical axis limits to provide some breathing room
ax.set_xlim(df['megapixels'].min() - 5, df['megapixels'].max() + 5)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['price_usd'].max() + 500)

# Improve the legend
# Move the legend outside the plot area to prevent it from overlapping with data
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the hue (sensor_type) and size (weight_grams) legends and give them titles
# The labels are split by index based on the number of unique hue categories
num_hues = len(df['sensor_type'].unique())
legend1 = ax.legend(h[:num_hues], l[:num_hues], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', title='Sensor Type', title_fontsize='14', fontsize='12')
ax.add_artist(legend1)
legend2 = ax.legend(h[num_hues:], l[num_hues:], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.65), loc='upper left', title='Weight (grams)', title_fontsize='14', fontsize='12')

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping, making space for the external legends
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95])

# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
